news_analysis.breaking_event_summary: A public advisory outlined key indicators to help consumers identify fraudulent text messages and avoid online scams.
news_analysis.retail_illusion: Do official-looking text messages about bank accounts or investments require immediate action to prevent financial loss?
news_analysis.institutional_reality: Urgent SMS prompts often spoof verified financial institutions; verifying details directly through official banking portals prevents unauthorized account compromise.
news_analysis.actionable_retail_rule: Never click embedded links in unsolicited SMS alerts regarding account status or transfers; verify notifications directly via your bank's official app or customer helpline.
news_analysis.editorial_directive: Frame the 7 signs as an active pre-transaction filter for retail investors receiving unverified SMS payment prompts. Avoid hypothetical loss calculations or sensational fear bait.

deck.caption:
A text arrives saying your bank account is suspended unless you click immediately. What should you do? Most digital fraud starts with artificial panic sent directly to your phone.

Here is how to spot the trap:
• Why genuine banks never threaten immediate account closure via SMS
• The 7 warning signs of spoofed payment requests and fake KYC alerts
• The zero-click rule to verify your money safely

Save this guide to protect your family from fraud, and share it with someone who manages money on their phone.

When you receive an urgent SMS about your account, do you check your passbook app directly, or do you click the message link first?

#OnlineFraud #BankingSafety #CyberSecurity #FinancialLiteracy

slides.headline: The panic trap behind sudden alerts

comparison_data.label: Scam SMS Claim
comparison_data.value: Your bank account will be blocked today unless you click immediately.

comparison_data.label: Banking Reality
comparison_data.value: Official banks give formal advance notice and never freeze accounts through an unverified text link.

slides.card_text: Scam SMS Claim Your bank account will be blocked today unless you click immediately. Banking Reality Official banks give formal advance notice and never freeze accounts through an unverified text link.

slides.headline: The danger inside embedded links
slides.card_text: Scam messages include links that look identical to your bank login portal. Clicking them directs you to a fake page designed to steal your account number, password, and mobile verification details.

checklist_data.text: Message comes from an ordinary 10-digit personal phone number
Sender name contains spelling mistakes or strange extra symbols
Official bank alerts use recognized registered business headers

slides.headline: Demands genuine institutions never make
slides.card_text: No legitimate bank or payment officer will ask for your secret PIN, UPI password, or OTP (One-Time Password) over text or a web form to keep your account active.

stat_data.label: Key indicators identified in fraud advisories
stat_data.context: Watch for sudden urgency, unknown sender numbers, embedded links, OTP requests, fake KYC warnings, suspicious attachments, and false prize offers.

flowchart_data.text: Close the SMS without tapping any links or calling sender numbers
Open your official banking app independently on your phone
Call the verified helpline number printed on your physical bank card or passbook

slides.title: Never let an urgent SMS dictate your financial decisions
slides.cta_detail: Save this checklist for the next time you get a suspicious alert, and verify all account status changes directly through your official banking portal.
